name: Mebolazine (Dymethazine)

lead: Mebolazine is an oral anabolic steroid that was once sold as a medicine and later withdrawn. It reappeared from about 2008 in gray-market supplements.

paras: It is reportedly a prodrug of methasterone, an androgen receptor agonist.
The FDA has acted against makers of supplements containing it, and it is classed with hepatotoxic oral steroids. Human safety data are absent.

lead: Mebolazine, also called dimethazine or dymethazine, is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid. It is a 17α-alkylated derivative of dihydrotestosterone and an unusual dimer of methasterone, two units joined by an azine group.[1]

Wikipedia reports that it reportedly acts as a prodrug of methasterone and that it was once marketed as the medicines Dostalon and Roxilon but is no longer sold.[1] Since about 2008 it has been found as an unlisted ingredient in some dietary supplements, and the US FDA has taken legal action against manufacturers of such products.[1]
No clinical trials were found. Published research is limited to metabolism studies.[1]

paras: It is classified as an androgen receptor agonist and is reported to act as a prodrug of methasterone.[1] A 2016 study examined its metabolism in vitro and in vivo.[1]

Wikipedia notes use since 2008 as an illegal ingredient in dietary supplements, including some sold as vitamin B products, with FDA legal action against makers.[1] A 2015 review in Andrology discussed the growing presence of designer androgens in over-the-counter supplements.[1] The article categorises it among hepatotoxins, consistent with concerns about oral 17α-alkylated steroids, but gives little detail.[1]

timeline.event: Begins to appear as an undeclared ingredient in dietary supplements.[1]
